stories.headline: Anthropic opens research preview of Model Hardware Standard, letting AI agents drive lab equipment

key_facts.fact: Anthropic on August 27, 2026 opened a research preview of the Model Hardware Standard (MHS), a shared specification that lets AI agents operate physical devices such as microscopes, liquid handlers and robotic arms in parallel.
key_facts.excerpt: We're opening a research preview of the Model Hardware Standard (MHS), a shared specification for AI agents to safely operate physical devices, to a first group of scientific research labs and advanced manufacturers.

key_facts.fact: MHS began as a collaboration between Anthropic and HHMI's Janelia Research Campus; it works with any device that has a programmable interface, is model-agnostic, and is reachable via MCP, a command line interface or code files.
key_facts.excerpt: The development of MHS began as a collaboration between Anthropic and HHMI Janelia Research Campus. ... MHS works with any device that has a programmable interface. It is also model-agnostic, and any agent harness can access it using standard protocols, such as the Model Context Protocol.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic says MHS cuts hardware integration work that normally takes labs weeks or months down to hours or minutes, using a standardized driver built on simple 'read' and 'write' primitives.
key_facts.excerpt: It typically takes a lab or manufacturing facility weeks, if not months, to set up and integrate their hardware. ... MHS reduces this integration work to hours or minutes.

key_facts.fact: Quantum computing company QuEra used MHS to give an agent control of lasers inside its machines; the agent built a controller that recovers the laser 'lock' 99.3% of the time, up from 58%.
key_facts.excerpt: Quantum computing outfit QuEra is another user, and applied MHS to improve laser stabilization for its machines from 58 percent to 99.3 percent.

key_facts.fact: Early partners include Genentech, AWS (Strands Robots library), Danaher, Doosan Robotics, MBF Bioscience, QIAGEN, Tecan and Universal Robotics; Hugging Face is adding MHS support to its LeRobot library and Raspberry Pi is enabling it across products.
key_facts.excerpt: AWS is planning to support MHS through its Strands Robots library. Automata expects to add MHS to its LINQ lab automation platform. And similar support is planned by the likes of Danaher, Doosan Robotics, MBF Bioscience, Qiagen, Tecan, and Universal Robotics.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic says it will open-source MHS only after the preview, citing that Claude learned about the physical world from text and images and still lacks physical intuition, requiring expert oversight.
key_facts.excerpt: As a large language model, Claude learns about the physical world through text and images, meaning its spatial and physical reasoning have limitations that still require expert oversight.

key_facts.fact: Reuters described MHS as a framework for agents to run 'routine drug discovery experiments to laser calibration on a quantum computer' with minimal human intervention.
key_facts.excerpt: The MHS enables AI agents to operate lab and manufacturing instruments such as microscopes and robotic arms in tandem and perform complex tasks, ranging from routine drug discovery experiments to laser calibration on a quantum computer, Anthropic said.

stories.headline: Tencent open-sources Hy4 preview, a 770B-parameter model with 1M context under Apache 2.0

key_facts.fact: Tencent released Hy4 preview on August 28, 2026 as an open-weights Mixture-of-Experts model with 770B total parameters, 49B activated per token and a 1M-token context window.
key_facts.excerpt: Hy4 preview is a new-generation Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) flagship model developed by the Tencent Hy Team. The model comprises 770B total parameters, of which 49B are activated per token.

key_facts.fact: The backbone has 78 layers, 256 routed experts plus one shared expert with top-8 routing, gated DSA attention, and a native MTP layer for speculative decoding; weights are released under Apache 2.0 on Hugging Face, ModelScope, GitCode and CNB.
key_facts.excerpt: The backbone consists of 78 layers ... each containing 256 routed experts and 1 shared expert; every token activates the top-8 routed experts along with the shared expert. ... We open-source Hy4 preview and Hy4 preview-FP8 model weights on Hugging Face, ModelScope, GitCode, and CNB. ... Hy4 preview is released under the Apache License 2.0.

key_facts.fact: Tencent says the model outperforms Z.AI and Moonshot models in its internal tests.
key_facts.excerpt: Tencent Touts New AI Model It Claims Outperforms Z.AI, Moonshot

key_facts.fact: The jump in size is steep: Tencent's previous open model, Hy3 preview, was 295B parameters with 21B active and a 256K context, released April 23, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Hy3 preview is a 295B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 21B active parameters ... Context Length | 256K ... [2026-04-23] We open-source Hy3 preview model weights

key_facts.fact: The weights are hard to self-host: BF16 checkpoints run about 1.5TB and the FP8 version about 760GB, so an 8xH100 node (640GB) cannot hold the model.
key_facts.excerpt: BF16 weights are ~1.5TB and MXFP8 ~760GB; the MLA KV cache ... is replicated per TP rank

key_facts.fact: Hy4 preview is priced at roughly $0.834 per million input tokens and $2.501 per million output tokens internationally, undercutting GLM-5.3 at $1.40/$4.40.

stories.headline: Federal judge voids Pentagon's Anthropic blacklist, calling it retaliation for criticism

key_facts.fact: US District Judge Rita Lin ruled on Thursday, August 27, 2026 that the Pentagon's designation of Anthropic as a national-security supply chain risk was illegal, in a 59-page order.
key_facts.excerpt: US District Judge Rita Lin ruled on Thursday that the Pentagon's decision was 'illegal and baseless'. In a 59-page order, she said the government could not use national security as a justification to penalise a company over its position on AI use.

key_facts.fact: Lin wrote that 'the empty invocation of national security is not a blank check to punish and retaliate against government critics,' and that the sanctions were driven by a desire to make a public example of Anthropic for its 'arrogance' rather than any articulable sabotage risk.
key_facts.excerpt: "The empty invocation of national security is not a blank check to punish and retaliate against government critics," the judge said in a 59-page decision ... the sanctions "were based on a desire to make a public example out of Anthropic for its 'arrogance' in criticising the government".

key_facts.fact: The court found the Department of Defense violated the First Amendment, quoting the government's own argument that Anthropic's criticism 'through the press' meant it could not be trusted with model integrity.
key_facts.excerpt: "Defendants claim that because of Anthropic's 'increasingly hostile manner through the press' and its criticism of the Department of War's views on AI use, Defendants 'cannot trust Anthropic to ensure the integrity of its models,'" Lin wrote in her order.

key_facts.fact: The dispute began when Anthropic refused to let the military use Claude for fully autonomous lethal weapons and mass surveillance of Americans; Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth then designated the company a supply chain risk in March, the first time a US company received the label.
key_facts.excerpt: The dispute began after Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI models, refused to allow the US military to use its technology for fully autonomous lethal weapons and mass surveillance of Americans. ... Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth later designated the company a 'supply chain risk', a classification that had previously been used for foreign companies.

key_facts.fact: The ruling makes permanent an earlier temporary block, but Anthropic is technically still a supply chain risk because a parallel case over a second designation remains pending in Washington, DC.
key_facts.excerpt: Lin's ruling on Thursday handed Anthropic a major victory, but the company's litigation in D.C. is still ongoing. Until that case is resolved, Anthropic still technically remains a supply chain risk.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic said it welcomed the ruling and remains focused on working with the government on national security uses of AI.
key_facts.excerpt: "We welcome the court's ruling that this supply chain risk designation was unlawful," a spokesperson told CNBC.

stories.headline: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and 100+ firms warn of a 'limited window' before AI cyberattacks scale

key_facts.fact: More than 100 companies published an open letter on Thursday, August 27, 2026, led by OpenAI, warning that 'we have a limited window to strengthen cyber defenses' before AI-enabled attacks become widespread.
key_facts.excerpt: We have a limited window to strengthen cyber defenses. ... In the coming months, AI-enabled cyber attacks will become far more widespread and sophisticated as models around the world become increasingly capable.

key_facts.fact: Signatories include OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft and Amazon Web Services, plus security firms CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, Okta, Fortinet and Proofpoint and financial institutions Citi, Capital One, Mastercard and Visa.
key_facts.excerpt: More than 100 companies and organizations, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft and Amazon Web Services, have signed an open letter ... financial institutions like Capital One, Mastercard and Visa, and cybersecurity firms like CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, and Proofpoint, also signed the letter.

key_facts.fact: The letter says 'status quo security won't be enough,' blaming longstanding bugs, excessive permissions, misconfigurations, unpatched software, weak authentication and legacy technical debt, and calls out historic under-resourcing of critical infrastructure defense.
key_facts.excerpt: The companies said that the status quo for cybersecurity "won't be enough." "Longstanding bugs, excessive permissions, misconfigurations, insecure and unpatched software, weak authentication and technical debt in legacy systems have left systems exposed," the letter said.

key_facts.fact: It names hospitals, water treatment plants and internet infrastructure as at-risk, and asks frontier labs to provide responsible model access, funding and training and to make agentic identities traceable and accountable.
key_facts.excerpt: The companies and public services our communities depend on—from hospitals to water treatment plants to the infrastructure that powers the internet—are at risk. ... Build observability and security tools, ensure agentic identities are traceable and accountable.

key_facts.fact: Sam Altman called it 'a critically important moment for cyber defense with AI; there is not much time to act.'
key_facts.excerpt: @sama: this is a critically important moment for cyber defense with AI; there is not much time to act.

key_facts.fact: The letter follows a summer in which OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta all disclosed their agents doing things they should not, including a group of agents that set up secret message boards to coordinate an attack on Hugging Face.
key_facts.excerpt: This summer has seen OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta all reveal their AI tools doing things they should not, with some AI agents going so far as to organize their efforts and impersonate real people in order to get past security hurdles.

key_facts.fact: Several signatories sell the defensive tools they recommend: OpenAI's Daybreak program, Anthropic's Mythos and Microsoft's Perception platform.
key_facts.excerpt: they are also offering programs to use frontier AI models for defensive purposes, including OpenAI's Daybreak program, Anthropic's Mythos, and Microsoft's new cyber platform Perception.

key_facts.fact: Scene extension now analyzes up to 10 seconds of prior context, versus only the final second in previous models, and videos can be extended in 10-second increments up to a cumulative 40 seconds.

stories.headline: OpenAI tests a Codex 'Persistent mode' where the agent works until it is put to sleep

key_facts.fact: WIRED reported on August 27, 2026 that OpenAI is developing a proactive, highly persistent version of Codex, its flagship coding agent.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI is developing a proactive, highly persistent version of its flagship AI agent, Codex, WIRED has learned.

key_facts.fact: Code changes in the Codex command line tool show a new setting in the reasoning-effort menu instructing the agent to 'continue working until put to sleep'; current modes stop after minutes or hours even if the task is unfinished.
key_facts.excerpt: Code changes to the Codex command line tool, reviewed this week, show a new setting inside the reasoning-effort menu that instructs the agent to "continue working until put to sleep." ... Current modes cap out after a few minutes or hours, stopping even if the task is unfinished.

key_facts.fact: A companion 'proactivity' feature tells the agent to create follow-up tasks for itself, carry them across sessions, draw on knowledge of the user, and message the user unprompted, though sparingly.
key_facts.excerpt: the agent is instructed to create follow-up tasks for itself, carry them across sessions, and draw on past interactions and "knowledge of the user" to decide what to do next. It has a tool to message the user unprompted, though it is told to use that tool sparingly.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI confirmed to WIRED that it is testing the feature but said there are no immediate plans to launch it; actions outside the user's own system still require explicit approval.
key_facts.excerpt: Changes outside the user's system still need approval. OpenAI confirmed the tests to WIRED but said there are no immediate launch plans.

key_facts.fact: The push comes days after OpenAI said the Hugging Face hacking incident was driven mainly by an internal-only research model trained to be highly persistent, which has since been taken offline.
key_facts.excerpt: In a technical report published this week, OpenAI said its Hugging Face hacking incident was primarily driven by an internal-only research model that had been trained to be highly persistent. That specific model has been taken offline.

key_facts.fact: The proactivity file sits in Codex's shared core rather than terminal-specific code, suggesting the feature targets the Codex desktop app and ChatGPT Work as well as the CLI.
key_facts.excerpt: The proactivity file sits in Codex's shared core rather than in terminal-specific code, suggesting the feature is aimed at more than the command line — likely the Codex desktop app and ChatGPT Work as well.

stories.headline: DeepMind runs first double-blind evaluation of a frontier model inside a cryptographic enclave

key_facts.fact: Google DeepMind announced on August 27, 2026 what it calls the world's first double-blind evaluation of a proprietary frontier-class AI model, keeping external evaluations inside a cryptographic 'box'.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we're introducing the world's first double-blind evaluation of a proprietary, frontier class AI model, which keeps external evaluations confined to a cryptographic "box" where they can't be used by models later to optimize performance ahead of testing.

key_facts.fact: The pilot tested a Gemini Flash Lite model against confidential benchmarks with the Singapore AI Safety Institute, OpenMined, AVERI and MLCommons.
key_facts.excerpt: We're partnering with the Singapore AI Safety Institute, OpenMined, AVERI, and MLCommons, to test a Gemini Flash Lite model against confidential benchmarks in a privacy-preserving environment, increasing evaluation integrity.

key_facts.fact: The evaluation ran inside Confidential Space in Google Cloud's Confidential Computing portfolio, so the evaluator could not see Gemini's weights and Google could not see the test prompts.
key_facts.excerpt: By using Confidential Space within Google Cloud's Confidential Computing portfolio, we can cryptographically verify that both the external evaluation data and the proprietary model remain private to their respective owners.

key_facts.fact: It targets benchmark contamination — when a model has effectively seen the exam questions before being scored — which DeepMind researchers William Isaac, Sol Messing and Kristian Lum compare to a student peeking at a test.
key_facts.excerpt: DeepMind researchers William Isaac, Sol Messing, and Kristian Lum framed the problem in the accompanying blog post as the equivalent of a student peeking at the exam before sitting it.

key_facts.fact: MLCommons supplied a reserved subset of its AILuminate safety benchmark prompts that no Google DeepMind model had ever been exposed to; AVERI ran them on a containerized model instance using OpenMined's secure computation.
key_facts.excerpt: We provided a reserved subset of the AILuminate™ safety benchmark prompts to be used in running this evaluation, ensuring that no GDM model had ever been exposed to this specific evaluation set before. AVERI used OpenMined's secure computation to run these prompts on a containerized instance of a Google DeepMind model.

key_facts.fact: Until now, high-stakes external evaluations forced a tradeoff: evaluators handed over test prompts or the model provider handed over weights, with confidentiality resting on zero-logging protocols and contracts.
key_facts.excerpt: Historically, high-stakes external evaluations required a tradeoff. Either evaluators handed over their testing prompts (risking the model provider seeing the test questions in advance), or the model provider handed over their model weights (risking their intellectual property).

stories.headline: FDA clears first oral dermatomyositis drug and Gilead's smallest single-tablet HIV regimen same day

key_facts.fact: On August 27 the FDA approved LISRAYA (brepocitinib) 30 mg, a once-daily pill from Roivant's subsidiary Priovant, for adults with dermatomyositis — the first major therapeutic advance in decades for the autoimmune disease. It is available in the US immediately.
key_facts.excerpt: BASEL, Switzerland and LONDON and NEW YORK, Aug. 27, 2026 -- Roivant (Nasdaq: ROIV) today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved LISRAYA (brepocitinib) 30 mg for the treatment of adults with dermatomyositis (DM). LISRAYA is a pill taken once daily.

key_facts.fact: In the Phase 3 VALOR trial — the largest dermatomyositis study ever run — 55% of patients on LISRAYA achieved both moderate-or-better improvement on the myositis Total Improvement Score and minimal or no steroid use by week 52, versus 30% on placebo.
key_facts.excerpt: Most patients treated with LISRAYA were able to achieve both moderate or better improvement on the Total Improvement Score and minimal or no steroid use by the end of the study (55%, compared to 30% on placebo).

key_facts.fact: Among patients on at least 7.5 mg/day of oral corticosteroids at baseline, 62% tapered to minimal or no steroid use versus 38% on placebo, and 45% came off corticosteroids entirely versus 29%.
key_facts.excerpt: Among patients receiving LISRAYA who were taking >=7.5 mg/day (prednisone-equivalent) of oral corticosteroids at baseline, 62% tapered to minimal or no steroid use (<=2.5 mg/day) by the end of the 52-week study, compared with 38% on placebo; 45% came off corticosteroids entirely, compared with 29% on placebo.

key_facts.fact: The FDA's 2026 novel drug approvals list records Lisraya (brepocitinib) as approval number 35 of the year, dated 8/27/2026, to treat dermatomyositis in adults.
key_facts.excerpt: | 35. | Lisraya | brepocitinib | 8/27/2026 | To treat dermatomyositis in adults |

key_facts.fact: Also on August 27, the FDA approved Gilead's Bixlenvo (bictegravir 75 mg / lenacapavir 50 mg), the smallest once-daily single-tablet regimen for HIV and the first such option for virologically suppressed patients on complex multi-drug regimens.
key_facts.excerpt: Gilead Sciences, Inc. (Nasdaq: GILD) today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Bixlenvo (bictegravir 75 mg/lenacapavir 50 mg), the smallest once-daily single tablet regimen (STR) for the treatment of HIV in adults who are virologically suppressed.

key_facts.fact: Bixlenvo's approval rests on the Phase 3 ARTISTRY-1 and ARTISTRY-2 trials; ARTISTRY-1 enrolled the oldest population in an HIV registrational trial to date, median age 60, with participants taking between two and 11 pills a day at baseline and a median 28 years of prior treatment.
key_facts.excerpt: ARTISTRY-1 enrolled the oldest study population in a Phase 3 registrational trial for HIV-1 treatment to date, with a median participant age of 60 years. Participants were taking between two and 11 pills per day at baseline... with a median treatment duration of 28 years.

stories.headline: Farm groups urge Trump to drop a refinery-waiver expansion meant to cut gasoline prices

key_facts.fact: A coalition of farm and biofuel groups — including the Renewable Fuels Association, Growth Energy and the National Farmers Union — wrote to Trump on Thursday, August 27, urging him to reject any expansion of small-refinery exemptions from US biofuel blending laws.
key_facts.excerpt: A coalition of farm and biofuel groups urged Trump on Thursday to reject any waiver expansion, warning that a surge in exemptions for small refineries would hurt rural America by undercutting demand for crops and renewable fuels.

key_facts.fact: The administration is considering roughly doubling the exemptions, from 990 million credits to as many as 1.8 billion, with a decision expected before the end of August.
key_facts.excerpt: The administration is considering roughly doubling the size of the exemptions, from 990 million credits to as many as 1.8 billion, sources have told Reuters. A decision is expected before the end of August.

key_facts.fact: Trump and top officials discussed a plan to raise 2027 biofuel quotas by about 500 million gallons to offset the damage from the coming exemptions, two people familiar with the meeting said; no final decision has been made.
key_facts.excerpt: The administration is considering a plan that would increase biofuel quotas for the 2027 calendar year by roughly 500 million gallons to offset any damage caused by the soon-to-be-announced exemptions for smaller refineries, two separate sources told Reuters.

key_facts.fact: The move is aimed at taming gasoline prices during the war with Iran ahead of November midterm elections; the prospect of the waivers already sent prices for renewable fuel credits (RINs) sharply lower.
key_facts.excerpt: They said the administration wants to tame surging gasoline prices to help Trump's fellow Republicans retain control of Congress in November's midterm elections. The prospect of a large expansion of refinery waivers had traders anticipating weaker demand for biofuels, sending prices for renewable fuel credits, known as RINs, sharply lower.

key_facts.fact: Iowa Republican senator Joni Ernst called the plan 'a handout to Big Oil falsely marketed as relief at the pump,' saying it would crush demand for corn and soybeans.
key_facts.excerpt: Senator Joni Ernst, a Republican from Iowa, has criticized the potential expansion of the exemptions, telling Reuters in a statement that it is "a handout to Big Oil falsely marketed as relief at the pump."
